story.title: Milo, Juno, and the Dinosaur Brick
story.subtitle: A dino-sized trip back in time.

chapters.heading: Chapter 1: The Three-Horned Friend
chapters.text:
Milo and Juno sat on their bedroom carpet. Their LEGO tower stood by the window. It was the tower from last night. The last brick had gone CLICK and held.

Juno patted the top brick. "It's so tall," she said.

Then the littlest brick began to glow. It glowed red, like a stop light. CLICK, CLICK, CLICK!

"The magic brick!" said Milo.

WHOOOOSH! The carpet spun like a teacup ride. The window turned green, then brown, then gone.

When Milo opened his eyes, tall ferny plants stood all around. The air smelled like rain.

THUMP. THUMP. THUMP. Something big was walking close by.

A huge animal stepped out. It had three horns on its face. It had a big bone shield around its neck, called a **frill**, like a shield for protection.

Juno counted on her fingers. "One horn, two horns, three horns!"

The brick blinked once. Yes!

"That's a **Triceratops**," said Milo. "I saw a picture in my book."

The Triceratops gave a soft snort and munched some leaves. She was big, but gentle.

"Dinosaurs started a really, really long time ago," Milo said, "before even Grandpa's grandpa's grandpa."

The brick blinked twice, and tiny glowing numbers appeared: 230 million.

"That means **230 million years** ago," Milo whispered. "That's SO many years, that's a big, big number!"

"A scientist named **Richard Owen** even gave dinosaurs their name," Milo remembered. "**Dinosaur** means 'terrible lizard' in an old language."

Juno giggled. "Terrible lizard! That's a silly name for such a nice lady."

The Triceratops gave a happy snort, right on cue, like she agreed.

Milo spotted huge footprints trailing off into the ferns. "Let's follow them and see who else is out here!"

"THREE HORNS!" Juno shouted, waving goodbye to her new friend.

chapters.heading: Chapter 2: The Giant Teeth
chapters.text:
Footprints as big as trash can lids dotted the mud. "Let's follow them!" said Milo.

They tiptoed through tall trees. Up ahead, something gave a big, sleepy ROOOOAR. It was just a yawn, not a scary roar.

A gigantic dinosaur stretched and opened its mouth wide. Its teeth were huge, pointy, and white.

"SO BIG TEETH!" Juno shouted.

Milo gasped. "Those teeth are bigger than my whole arm!"

The brick blinked a number. "Some teeth were almost **12 inches** long," Milo said, "that's as long as a school ruler, root and all!"

Juno hid behind Milo's leg for one second, then peeked out. "Is it going to eat us?"

Milo shook his head. "Nope. Its mouth is closed now. See? Just a big sleepy yawn."

The dinosaur blinked slowly and lay back down in the sun.

"That's a **Tyrannosaurus rex**," Milo said. "T-rex for short. Like a shark's tooth, but even bigger!"

The brick lit up with a tiny picture of bones in a museum.

"One T-rex skeleton is named **Sue**," Milo remembered. "People found her bones in **South Dakota**, in **1990**. She's one of the biggest T-rex skeletons ever found!"

Juno waved at the sleepy dinosaur. "Night night, Sue's cousin!"

The T-rex gave a tiny snore. HRRRRRR.

Milo and Juno giggled and tiptoed away, careful not to wake her again.

chapters.heading: Chapter 3: Spikes and Plates
chapters.text:
Next, the footprints turned into giant round prints, side by side.

A dinosaur with big, pointy plates down its back shuffled by. The plates looked like a row of giant triangle stickers.

"Whoa, it's wearing spiky armor!" said Milo.

Juno pointed at its tail. "What are THOSE for?"

Long spikes stuck out of the tail's end.

The brick blinked, and a funny word popped up: thagomizer.

"That spiky tail has a silly name," Milo said. "Scientists call it a **thagomizer**, a spiky tail for keeping safe. Say that three times fast!"

Juno tried. "Thaga-miser, thaga-mixer, thaga-mizzle!" She giggled so hard she fell over.

The Stegosaurus swished its tail gently, nowhere near the kids, and kept munching ferns.

"I bet the spikes helped keep it safe," Milo said.

The brick blinked once. Yes!

"This is a **Stegosaurus**," said Milo. "Big plates on top, spiky tail at the end."

Juno stood up, dusted off her knees, and bowed to the Stegosaurus. "Nice armor, Stegosaurus!"

The dinosaur gave a slow blink back, like it understood every word.

chapters.heading: Chapter 4: The Good Mother
chapters.text:
Past the ferns, they found a cozy nest made of mud and leaves.

Round eggs sat inside, and a mama dinosaur curled around them.

"Shh," whispered Milo. "Let's not scare her."

Juno tiptoed closer, just to look, not to touch. "BABY DINOSAURS!"

The mama lifted her head and gave a gentle grumble, then settled back down.

"This dinosaur is called **Maiasaura**," Milo said. "Her name even means 'good mother lizard.'"

The brick blinked a picture of more nests, all in a row.

"Scientists found lots of nests like this in a place called **Montana**," Milo added. "That told them dinosaur moms took care of their babies, just like our mom takes care of us."

Juno peeked at the eggs, careful to stay back. "They're round like eggs from the fridge, but bumpy!"

Juno smiled and waved softly. "Bye bye, good mama. Take care of your eggs!"

They backed away slowly, quiet as mice, and let the mama rest.

"That was the gentlest dinosaur yet," Milo whispered.

chapters.heading: Chapter 5: Turkey-Sized Surprise
chapters.text:
Something rustled in the bushes. RUSTLE, RUSTLE, RUSTLE.

"Uh oh," said Milo. "In my movies, this dinosaur is as big as a car!"

Out popped a dinosaur... about the size of a turkey.

Juno burst out laughing. "That's not scary, that's tiny!"

It had feathers all over, fluffy like a big chicken.

"That's a **Velociraptor**," said Milo, surprised. "But it's so small! And feathery!"

The brick blinked, showing a tiny glowing feather.

"Lots of dinosaurs had **feathers**," Milo said, "even scary-sounding ones like this."

The little Velociraptor cocked its head and clucked, almost like a bird.

Juno leaned in close, careful not to touch, just to look. "It sounds like a chicken!"

"That's because birds today came from dinosaurs like this one," Milo said. "So really, dinosaurs never totally went away. Some turned into birds!"

Juno looked up at a bird flying overhead. "Hi, dino-bird!"

The Velociraptor fluffed its feathers proudly and strutted off into the bushes.

chapters.heading: Chapter 6: The Longest Neck
chapters.text:
The ground rumbled. RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE.

A neck as tall as the tallest ferns came into view.

"Whoa," breathed Milo. "That neck goes on FOREVER."

The whole dinosaur kept coming, and coming, and coming.

Juno's mouth fell open. "It's the biggest one yet!"

"This might be **Argentinosaurus**," Milo said, "maybe the longest dinosaur that ever lived!"

The brick blinked a number: 100. "Some scientists think it was over **100 feet** long," Milo said. "That's like counting 100 of your own big steps in a row!"

The giant dinosaur lowered its head and gave the kids a gentle, curious look.

Juno waved both arms. "Hi, giant dinosaur! You're SO long!"

The dinosaur let out a low, friendly rumble back, like a giant's hello.

"I bet it eats a LOT of leaves to grow that big," said Milo.

The dinosaur plucked a huge mouthful of leaves from the treetop, proving him right.

chapters.heading: Chapter 7: Dinosaur Clues in the Sand
chapters.text:
WHOOOOSH! The ferns turned to sand. They stood in a desert full of sandy hills.

"This is the **Gobi Desert**," Milo said, remembering his dinosaur book. "Scientists find tons of dinosaur bones here!"

People in hats knelt in the sand, brushing dirt off big bones with tiny brushes.

"They're bone scientists," Milo told Juno. "They dig up old dinosaur bones to learn how dinosaurs lived."

Juno picked up a stick and started "digging" in the sand too. "I'm a bone digger too!"

One scientist smiled and showed them a footprint pressed into hard stone.

"Old bones and footprints can turn into stone over a really, really long time," Milo explained. "That stone picture is called a **fossil**."

Juno put her own foot next to the stone footprint. "Mine's way smaller!"

"I heard a story once," Milo said, "that a farmer's dog found part of a famous dinosaur by digging in the dirt. That part might just be a fun story people like to tell, not something that really happened. But it's still a fun one!"

The scientist nodded and waved as they packed up more bones, carefully, to study back home.

Juno found a tiny pointy rock. "Is THIS a fossil?"

The scientist laughed kindly. "Maybe! Let's find out together."

Milo grinned. "Finding dinosaur clues is the best job ever."

chapters.heading: Chapter 8: Four Little Wings
chapters.text:
A tiny dinosaur leaped off a branch above them.

It didn't fall. It GLIDED, like a paper airplane, all the way to the next tree.

"Whoa, it's flying!" Juno shouted.

"Look closer," said Milo. "I count... one, two, three, four wings!"

Two wings were on its arms. Two more were on its legs.

"That's a **Microraptor**," Milo said. "Four wings helped it glide from tree to tree, like gliding on a zipline!"

The brick blinked happily, showing little glowing wing shapes.

Juno flapped her own arms like wings and ran in a circle. "I'm gliding too! WHOOOOSH!"

The Microraptor landed on a branch, tilted its head, and chirped, almost like it was cheering her on.

It glided one more time, soaring over their heads before landing softly in the leaves.

"Best four-winged dinosaur ever," Milo said, giving it a little wave.

chapters.heading: Chapter 9: Back Home, Changed Forever
chapters.text:
The red brick blinked three times. Time to go home!

Before they left, the ground rumbled one more time, but gently, like the end of a bedtime story.

"A really, really long time ago," Milo said, "about **66 million years**, something big happened, and most dinosaurs disappeared."

Juno looked worried for just a second. "Disappeared? Like, gone?"

"But not totally gone," Milo said quickly, smiling. "Remember the dino-bird? Some dinosaurs turned into birds, and birds are still flying around today!"

Juno brightened. "So dinosaurs are kind of still here!"

"Exactly," said Milo, and the Triceratops, the T-rex, the Stegosaurus, and even the littlest Microraptor all seemed to nod in the fading light.

WHOOOOSH! The world spun, green and brown and gone, and the carpet appeared beneath them again.

They were home, right where their LEGO tower still stood.

On the very top brick sat something new: one tiny, soft feather.

Juno held it up. "A dino feather! For our tower!"

Milo gently placed the feather beside the top brick. It stayed, perfectly still.

The red brick gave one last happy CLICK, then its glow faded to sleep.

"Play well, dinosaurs," Juno whispered.

Milo yawned and hugged his sister. "Best adventure yet."

story.ending_line: Goodnight, Milo. Goodnight, Juno. Play well.

true_facts.text: Dinosaurs first showed up a really, really long time ago — about **230 million years** ago!
**Triceratops** has three horns on its face and a big bone shield called a **frill**.
A **T-rex** tooth could be almost **12 inches** long, root and all — longer than a school ruler!
One famous T-rex skeleton is named **Sue**. She was found in **South Dakota** in **1990**.
**Stegosaurus** had big plates on its back and a spiky tail scientists call a **thagomizer**.
A **Velociraptor** was only about the size of a **turkey** — way smaller than in the movies!
Lots of dinosaurs, even Velociraptor, had **feathers** just like birds.
Birds flying around today came from dinosaurs, so dinosaurs never totally disappeared!
**Maiasaura** dinosaur moms took care of their babies in nests, like the ones found in **Montana**.
**Argentinosaurus** might be the longest dinosaur ever — over **100 feet** long!
**Microraptor** had **four wings** and could glide from tree to tree.
About **66 million years** ago, most dinosaurs disappeared — but some turned into birds.
Old bones and footprints can turn into stone over a long, long time — that stone picture is called a **fossil**.

bible_suggestions.ending_summary: They came home to find a tiny dinosaur feather resting beside the top brick of their still-standing LEGO tower.

story.title: Sam and Sticky's Wall-Climbing Night
story.subtitle: A tiny adventure with gecko toes, spider hairs, and one very slow snail.

chapters.heading: Chapter 1: Sticky Wakes Up
chapters.text:
Sam knelt in the backyard grass, holding a jar with a small, fuzzy spider inside. "Hello, friend," Sam whispered. "I'll just look, then let you go."

Mom called from the door. "Bedtime, Sam! Jar down, please, and come wash up."

Sam set the jar on his windowsill, lid loose, and climbed into bed. On the shelf sat a little green gecko nightlight, a gift from Grandma. It had never done anything but glow.

Tonight, it blinked. Then it winked.

"Well, hello," said a small, raspy voice. "I'm Sticky. I've been waiting for someone who likes bugs as much as you do."

Sam sat straight up. "You're... talking?"

"I'm a gecko," Sticky said. "Geckos know every trick there is for climbing walls. Want to see?"

"YES," Sam said, maybe a little too loud.

Sticky's green glow grew brighter and brighter, filling the whole room like a puddle of moonlight. Sam felt his whole body go light as a leaf.

SHRINK! Sam was suddenly the size of a bottle cap, standing right beside the jar he'd left on the sill.

"Whoa," Sam said, looking up at the window glass, which now looked as tall as a mountain. "Everything is so big."

"Not for long," said Sticky, scuttling straight up the glass like it was flat ground. "Follow me. Tonight, you learn how every climbing creature on Earth gets up a wall."

Sam reached out and touched the glass. His fingers didn't stick at all. He slid right back down. "Ow. How do YOU do that?"

Sticky grinned, which is a tricky thing for a gecko to do. "That," he said, "is lesson one."

chapters.heading: Chapter 2: The Gecko's Secret Feet
chapters.text:
Sticky flattened one foot against the glass. "Look close," he said.

Sam pressed his nose near Sticky's toes and saw rows of lines, thinner than thread.

"Those are **millions of tiny hairs** on my toes," Sticky said. "So many, so small, you could never count them all."

"That's why you don't fall?" Sam asked.

"That's why," Sticky said. "The hairs grab the glass so gently, it isn't glue at all. No mess, no drips, ever."

Sam wiggled his own fingers. "Can I try?"

"Climbing powder," Sticky said, and sprinkled green dust over Sam's hands and feet.

Sam pressed his palm to the glass. It held! He pulled. It stuck! He gasped, pulled harder, and his hand peeled away like tape, easy as that.

"Whoa, whoa, WHOA!" Sam yelled, scrambling up the glass on hands and knees. Partway up, his foot slipped, just for a second, and his tummy did a little flip. Then his sticky fingers grabbed tight again, and he was fine.

"Told you," Sticky said, climbing up beside him. "Even I wobble sometimes. The trick is just to grab again."

At the top, Sam looked down at how far he'd come and grinned so wide his cheeks hurt. "I CLIMBED A WINDOW!"

"First of many," said Sticky. "Now, who do you think else can do this?"

Sam thought about something small and eight-legged, sitting in a jar not far away at all.

chapters.heading: Chapter 3: Eight Sticky Feet
chapters.text:
Sam hurried to the jar. Inside, the little spider was climbing the glass walls, round and round.

"Hey, I know her!" Sam said. "She climbs this jar all day long."

"Spiders have their own trick," Sticky said. "Look at her feet."

Sam leaned close. Tiny brushes of hair covered each of the spider's eight feet.

"Those are tiny hairs too," Sticky said, "a little like mine. That's why so many spiders can climb smooth glass, just like this jar."

"Eight sticky feet," Sam whispered. "That's so much grip."

The spider reached a smooth patch near the lid, and her feet began to slide.

"She's stuck!" Sam said.

"Not stuck, slipping," Sticky said. "Watch what she does."

The spider spread her feet wider, pressing more hairs flat against the glass, and found her grip again. She scuttled right over the smooth patch and out through a tiny gap Sam hadn't even noticed.

"She used MORE sticky hairs!" Sam said. "I bet that's the trick for tricky spots."

"Smart bug-watcher," Sticky said, bumping Sam's shoulder with his tail.

Sam opened the jar lid wide. "Go have your night, friend," he told the spider, and she scurried off into the grass.

"That's one," Sticky said. "Plenty more climbers to go. Ready?"

"EIGHT STICKY FEET!" Sam shouted, and ran after Sticky toward the porch light, where something small and buzzing kept bumping the glass.

chapters.heading: Chapter 4: The Buzzy, Glue-Foot Fly
chapters.text:
At the porch light, a fat little fly kept bumping the glass, sticking, then bumping again.

"Why does he keep smacking into it?" Sam asked, giggling.

"He's clumsy," Sticky admitted, "but his feet are clever. Flies have tiny pads that **ooze a sticky goo**, like one little drop of glue on each foot."

"Glue feet!" Sam said. "That's so weird and so cool."

The fly landed upside down on the porch ceiling and sat there like it was nothing at all.

"Look down," Sticky said. "See those tiny marks?"

Sam squinted. A trail of little dots led across the ceiling, glowing faintly in the moonlight.

"Footprints!" Sam said. "His sticky feet leave marks!"

"They do," Sticky said. "Watch where they go."

Sam followed the dots with his eyes, all the way to a crack in the ceiling boards. "There's a path! The fly found a secret way across the bumpy part!"

"Nice spotting," Sticky said. "Want to take his shortcut?"

Sam nodded, and climbing powder tingled on his fingers again. He pressed his hand to the first sticky dot, and sure enough, it held, just like the fly's trail promised it would.

They crossed the ceiling dot by dot, Sam laughing the whole way, until they reached the far wall, where something with six legs and tough little claws was already waiting for them.

chapters.heading: Chapter 5: Ants Change Their Tools
chapters.text:
An ant marched up the brick wall like it weighed nothing at all.

"Ants are climbers too?" Sam asked.

"The very best kind," Sticky said. "Watch her feet on the rough brick."

Sam saw tiny hooks, like little claws, digging into every bump.

"She's using claws," Sam said, "like a cat, but way tinier."

Then the ant reached a smooth painted stripe on the brick, and her claws found nothing to grab onto.

Sam gasped. "She's gonna—"

But the ant simply switched. Flat **sticky pads** popped out from her feet instead, and she walked right over the smooth stripe like it was no trouble.

"She switched her feet!" Sam said, eyes huge. "Claws for bumpy, sticky pads for smooth!"

"Exactly," Sticky said. "Ants and cockroaches both carry two tools, and pick whichever one the wall needs."

Right on cue, a cockroach scuttled past, claws out for the brick, pads out the moment it hit a smooth puddle of dried paint.

"They're like tiny toolboxes," Sam said.

Sticky laughed, a dry little chuckle. "Best way I've ever heard it put."

Sam clapped his hands, and somewhere above them, a much bigger shadow moved along the fence, something with hooves, not feet at all.

chapters.heading: Chapter 6: The Goat on the Steep Rock
chapters.text:
Sticky's green glow spread wide, like a window opening in the air. Through it, Sam saw steep gray rocks, higher than any wall he'd ever seen.

"Whoa," Sam breathed. "Can we go look?"

"Hold my tail," Sticky said, and they stepped through together.

A mountain goat stood on a rock so steep it looked like a wall tipped on its side. Sam's tummy did a little flip just watching. "Won't he fall?"

"Watch his feet," Sticky said.

The goat's hooves had a hard, curved edge around the outside, and a soft, squishy middle pressed flat against every bump.

"The edge grips," Sam guessed, "and the soft part kind of... hugs the rock?"

"Exactly right," Sticky said. "A hard rim outside, and a **soft, grippy pad** inside that molds to the rock like a glove."

The goat leapt to a ledge barely wider than Sam's hand, landed perfectly, and chewed some grass like nothing had happened at all.

"He's not even scared!" Sam laughed, his own tummy flip long gone.

"Goats climb cliffs like that every day," Sticky said. "No big deal, for a goat."

Sam waved at the goat from far away. "Nice jump, goat friend!"

The goat flicked an ear, and the green window began to close, pulling them gently back toward the porch.

chapters.heading: Chapter 7: Claws and Sticky Toes in the Backyard Tree
chapters.text:
Back on the porch, a squirrel zipped straight up the oak tree trunk, quick as a blink.

"How does he go that fast?" Sam asked.

"Sharp little claws," Sticky said. "Curved ones, that dig into cracks and bumps too tiny for you or me to even see."

Sam ran his fingers over the bark. It looked smooth from far away, but up close, it was full of tiny holes and ridges. "Oh! It's bumpier than it looks!"

"Exactly why claws work so well on bark," Sticky said.

Further up, on a wet leaf, sat a small green tree frog, its toes spread wide and flat.

"That frog's feet look different," Sam said. "Kind of... squishy and round."

"Tree frogs have flat, **sticky toe pads**," Sticky said, "covered in tiny little patterns, like the bumps on a soccer ball. Perfect for holding onto wet, slippery leaves."

Sam looked from the squirrel's sharp claws to the frog's soft, squishy toes. "So claws are for digging in, and sticky pads are for holding on wet, smooth stuff?"

"You just figured out two whole animal tricks in one breath," Sticky said. "Not bad, bug-watcher."

Sam beamed, and gave the tree frog a gentle, careful wave, careful never to touch it. "Night, little guy."

chapters.heading: Chapter 8: The Snail's Slow Slide (and Sam's Big Idea)
chapters.text:
Near the garden hose, a snail glided straight up the brick wall, slow and steady.

"He's not fast," Sam said, "but he's not falling either."

"Snails don't climb with hairs or pads," Sticky said. "They make their own **slime** and glide on it, gripping with a squishy foot underneath."

Sam watched the shiny trail glisten behind the snail. "That's kind of gross," he said, "but also kind of amazing."

"Both things can be true," Sticky agreed.

Sam sat back on his heels and thought about everyone he'd met tonight: hairy gecko toes, spider hairs, fly goo, ant claws and pads, goat hooves, squirrel claws, frog pads, and now snail slime.

"People don't have any of that," Sam said. "We just have plain old fingers."

"Not always," Sticky said, his eyes twinkling. "Some scientists loved gecko feet so much, they built their own sticky, gecko-style pads for human hands. In **2014**, a person used two of those pads to climb straight up a glass wall, just like a gecko."

Sam's mouth fell open. "A whole PERSON climbed a window?!"

"A whole person," Sticky said, "because they copied a gecko's trick."

"I want sticky gloves," Sam said firmly.

"Maybe you'll invent them one day," Sticky said, and his green glow began to shrink back down, carrying them both along with it.

POP! Sam landed back in his own bed, regular size, pajama sleeves rumpled. The nightlight sat quietly on the shelf, glowing its same soft green.

On the windowsill, the jar sat empty, lid open, just how Sam had left it.

Sam smiled and pulled up his blanket. "Climb well, Sticky," he whispered.

The little green gecko on the shelf blinked once, as if to say it right back.

story.ending_line: Goodnight, Sam. Climb well, and sleep tight.

true_facts.text: Geckos have **millions of tiny hairs** on their toes that help them climb glass and walk on ceilings.
A gecko's sticky grip isn't glue — it can **peel its toes off like tape** without leaving any mess.
Spiders have tiny hairs on their eight feet too, which is why many spiders can climb smooth glass.
Flies have feet that **ooze a sticky goo**, like a tiny drop of glue on each foot.
Ants and cockroaches use sharp little claws on bumpy walls, then switch to **sticky pads** on smooth walls.
Mountain goats climb steep cliffs with hooves that have a hard edge and a **soft, grippy pad** inside.
Squirrels climb trees using sharp, curved claws that dig into tiny bumps and cracks in the bark.
Tree frogs have **sticky toe pads** with tiny patterns that help them hold onto wet, slippery leaves.
Snails climb smooth walls by gliding along on their own **slime**, gripping with a squishy foot.
In **2014**, scientists built sticky, gecko-style pads that let a real person climb up a glass wall.
